title: the superclaude floor proof's uncreatable-path fixture is a path under a regular file, so it is absent on Windows as on Linux
intention: bin/proofs/test_superclaude_is_never_refused_by_the_floor.py builds UNCREATABLE as a path beneath a regular file it creates in a temp dir, which no host lets a directory be made under, in place of the Linux-only /proc path.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: test_the_negative_fixture_is_genuinely_absent / test_a_failed_lay_down_names_applys_cause failed with '/proc/cairn-no-such-dir/venv exists' on Windows
traces_to: Law 3: the 'exists' was measured as a directory left on disk by an earlier Windows run; Law 8: a fixture that cannot be absent makes every green under it hollow.
how: At line 36 replace the /proc literal with a path beneath a regular file made once in a temp dir (blocker.write_text, UNCREATABLE = (blocker / 'venv').as_posix()), kept for the run. Red-first proof bin/proofs/test_superclaude_floor_fixture_is_uncreatable_on_every_host.py holds two teeth that red on Linux against the unedited file: (1) an ast scan finds no string constant beginning /proc/ in bin/proofs/test_superclaude_is_never_refused_by_the_floor.py; (2) the proof module's UNCREATABLE has a parent that is a regular file, does not exist, and os.makedirs on it raises OSError.
